## My request:
Inspect Phase 5B’s `code/hybrid_core.py`, `code/benchmark.py`, move diagnostics, and tooling record. Determine whether PySDD supports correct local vtree moves on a live compiled SDD without recompiling the CNF for each candidate. Build a small exactness-checked prototype and compare move cost with fresh compilation. Report a concrete supported method or a tooling NO-GO. Do not retune or rerun the frozen held-out campaign, use semantic prime truth in objectives, or alter archived Phase 4/5 files.

items.text: I’ll check the draft generator, protocol, and runner together for contradictions or validity gaps. If the design holds up, I’ll freeze and run the campaign in Linux with the registered limits, keeping the raw results and stopping on any integrity failure. I’ll use the local Docker host, so no Runpod charge is needed.

items.text: The design review found no contradiction with the runner’s registered methods, limits, selection rule, or exactness checks. I updated the protocol to name the local Docker execution host and confirmed that only the generator changed since the Linux preflight; the tested worker and move code match their recorded hashes. I’m freezing and starting the formal sequence now.

The freeze succeeded on Linux. Its receipt records the source hashes, pinned environment, and a passing hard-cap check; validation has reached 150 of 252 planned worker trials with no reported exactness failure. I’m letting the registered sequence continue.
